newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 5.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 5.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 5.00 cents higher Wednesday after a drop in stocks certified for delivery against the exchange re-ignited supply concerns, traders said.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 13,999 bags to 27,699 bags as of May 5. There were 11,250 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

Tuesday, New York arabica futures ended sharply lower in a technical corection to the recent run-up. July ended down 5.65 cents at 212.85 cents a lb, toward the bottom of the day's 221.50 to 212.25 range. Spot May fell 1.30 cents to 249.60, while the back months closed 0.50 to 5.25 lower.

Technically, traders pegged July near-term resistance at 217.00 to 218.00, followed by yesterday's high of 221.50. On the downside, they said a breach of 211.50 to 209.00 support zone for July could lead to a test of the 200.00 mark.
On the fundamental front, Colombian truck drivers lifted their day-old strike in Cartagena port, partly dispelling fears that the work stoppage could spread nationwide.
LIFFE coffee futures were mixed early Wednesday after a weak start, with July up $10 at the midday break at $1,710, the day's high.
